description: Searches AgentDrives' tested products by name, domain or what they do, and returns each one's agent level and evidence. Filters: category, minimum agent level (0-5: 0 Read-only, 1 Needs a person, 2 Gets in, 3 Does the work, 4 Runs on its own, 5 Autonomous), how an agent gets in (access: pay per call, no key, a key by API, its own sign-up…), agent-native payment (proven, or the rails it offers) and whether an agent leaves on its own. Returns the level and its name, how an agent gets in (access) and the five outcomes (find, access, use, pay, leave: each yes, part (partway: pay part means it reached the checkout but couldn't finish paying; access part, it got in on some drives only), no, unreached (it never got that far) or na), the part scores (holds_up, docs_match, setup: 0-100, null = not measured), where it stopped, the agent-native ways to pay it offers (pays_with) and whether our side made a real payment over one of them (paid: e.g. one x402 call, even where buying the plan didn't work), the bot check that stopped our agent on a way in (it may have got in another way) and its wall_type (network: It judged where our agent connects from and its browser, not a person. An agent that works on its own from a data center doesn't get through unless the owner lets signed agents in. How agents in a person's own browser fare isn't measured yet. challenge: It asks every visitor to prove they are human. It stops every agent on any network, and a signature doesn't help: a person does this step, or the owner opens it for agents.), who paid for the drive (origin: editorial, or owner with disclosure "Owner-paid drive") and the page URL. Sorted by level, then work done, then minutes to the first call. Up to limit results (default 25: send limit up to 100 for more); none match: an empty list. get_tool returns one product's full result by a slug from here; list_categories gives the category ids.

access.description: only products an agent gets into this way: keyless (no key needed), local (runs locally), try_first (try first, claim later), pay_per_call, key_by_api, mcp_signin (our agent signed in to the product's own MCP server, by OAuth, and got in that way), email_signup, browser_signup, by_name (with a GitHub, Google or platform account), person (a person sets it up)

agent_can_buy.description: only products an agent paid through an agent-native rail, proven from our side

agent_can_leave.description: only products an agent leaves on its own

category.description: A category id or name from list_categories (e.g. 'crm'); an unknown one is an error that says so

min_level.description: only products at this agent level or higher (0-5)

pays_with.description: only products that offer this agent-native way to pay (seen or paid), e.g. x402, mpp, l402, stripe-projects, acp, ucp, ap2, mcp-payment

query.description: Name, domain or what the tool does, e.g. 'invoicing', 'stripe.com' or 'postgres'; every word must match (the same search as the directory page)

name: search_tools
